entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 4 Ro 4:1-25 . The Foregoing Doctrine of Justification by Faith Illustrated from the Old Testament. First: Abraham was justified by faith. 1-3. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16418"/><div sID="gen31866" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16418"/><hi type="bold">9-12. Cometh this blessedness then, &c.--</hi>that is, "Say not, All this is spoken of the circumcised, and is therefore no evidence of God's general way of justifying men; for Abraham's justification took place long before he was circumcised, and so could have no dependence upon that rite: nay, 'the sign of circumcision' was given to Abraham as 'a seal' (or token) of the (justifying) righteousness which he had before he was circumcised; in order that he might stand forth to every age as the parent believer--the model man of justification by faith--after whose type, as the first public example of it, all were to be moulded, whether Jew or Gentile, who should thereafter believe to life everlasting." <div eID="gen31866" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16419"/><div sID="gen31867" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16419"/><hi type="bold">13-15. For the promise, &c.--</hi>This is merely an enlargement of the foregoing reasoning, applying to the law what had just been said of circumcision.<div eID="gen31867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31868" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that he should be the heir of the world--</hi>or, that "all the families of the earth should be blessed in him."<div eID="gen31868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31869" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">was not to Abraham or to his seed through the law--</hi>in virtue of obedience to the law.<div eID="gen31869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31870" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">but through the righteousness of faith--</hi>in virtue of his simple faith in the divine promises. <div eID="gen31870" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 13-15. For the promise, &c.-- This is merely an enlargement of the foregoing reasoning, applying to the law what had just been said of circumcision. that he should be the heir of the world-- or, that "all the families of the earth should be blessed in him." was not to Abraham or to his seed through the law-- in virtue of obedience to the law. but through the righteousness of faith-- in virtue of his simple faith in the divine promises.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16422"/><div sID="gen31875" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16422"/><hi type="bold">16-17. Therefore, &c.--</hi>A general summary: "Thus justification is by faith, in order that its purely gracious character may be seen, and that all who follow in the steps of Abraham's faith--whether of his natural seed or no--may be assured of the like justification with the parent believer." <div eID="gen31875" type="x-p"/>
